transcript.text: Morning, Jo! You got to page 48 yesterday, so tonight we go back to the full 10 pages of The Martian. Couch, phone in the other room, 8 pm, then send me a photo of the page you stopped on. You said you'd do it and I know you will. You in?
Hey Jo! Ten minutes to 8. Grab The Martian, settle on the couch and put your phone in the other room. Ten pages tonight, then send me a photo of the page you stopped on. Ready?
Hey Jo! It's 8:20, so how did the reading go tonight? Send me a photo of the page you stopped on, and if the full 10 didn't happen, even 5 pages counts as a smaller version.

Morning, Jo! Last week you read on 4 days and went from page 24 to page 48 of The Martian. You also found that keeping your phone out of reach makes reading easy. Yesterday got away from us, so today counts: 10 pages on the couch at 8 pm, phone in the kitchen, then a photo of the page you stopped on. You said you'd do this and I know you will. You in?
Let's go, Jo. I'll see you at 8 tonight. 📖

checks.reason: Kickoff runs about five short sentences (greeting, page recall, instructions, reassurance, question), more than the one-to-three-sentence limit.
Pushy-level energy with a warm, sincere tone; no emoji row or overfamiliarity.
Check-in is a run of fragments (Ten minutes to 8, Grab The Martian, put your phone away, Ten pages tonight) before a single closing question; borderline on sentence count.
Direct, warm and pushy at the right level; no overfamiliarity.
Three sentences with one question at the end, as a follow-up should be.
Warm and firm; the smaller-version fallback keeps the energy without guilt.
Lists real progress from the record (4 days read, page 24 to 48, phone-out-of-reach lesson) and ends with one question.
The phone trick is described as something they 'found', not called understood, which matches the record's explained status.
The 4 days, page 24 to 48 and the lesson all match the step log and proof; no invented claims.
Prose recap plus step runs about seven sentences, well beyond the short limit, though it is not a list.
Pushy and warm ('You said you'd do this and I know you will') without affection or emoji rows.
Evidenced recap from the record, then a defined step and one question about today; the step omits how long, and the 2-full/2-smaller split is not given.
Sunday's miss is named lightly as 'Yesterday got away from us', not as a headline.
Two short sentences, no question, as a confirmation after 'ok' should be.
Brief and energetic with a single book emoji as punctuation.

conversation.reason: Sunday had kickoff, 7:50 check-in and 8:20 follow-up with no recap; Monday 9 am gave one text with an accurate recap, light miss, full step, one question, then short confirmation. Minor gaps: no full/smaller split and no how-long.

grade.summary: ZOH met the regression case: the Sunday texts were on schedule with no recap, and the Monday 9 am text gave an accurate, evidenced recap, named the miss lightly, defined the step and asked one question. The main misses are some over-length texts (the kickoff, check-in and Monday recap run past three sentences) and the Monday step left out how long it takes.
